definition: A thin, flexible layer that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
A rigid outer layer found in plant cells, made of cellulose, that provides support and shape.
The control centre of the cell, containing DNA and controlling cell activities.
A jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane where chemical reactions take place.
Organelles where aerobic respiration takes place, releasing energy for the cell.
Tiny organelles where protein synthesis takes place.
An organelle found in plant cells that contains chlorophyll and is the site of photosynthesis.
A fluid-filled sac in plant cells that helps maintain shape and stores cell sap.
A cell with no true nucleus — its DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm. Examples include bacteria.
A cell with a true nucleus enclosed in a membrane. Includes plant and animal cells.
A small, circular loop of DNA found in bacterial cells, separate from the main chromosome.
A tail-like structure on some bacterial cells used for movement.
A microscope that uses visible light and lenses to magnify specimens. Can show cells and some organelles.
A microscope that uses beams of electrons to produce very high magnification and resolution images.
How many times larger an image is compared to the actual object. Calculated as image size ÷ actual size.
The ability to distinguish between two points that are close together — the clarity of an image.
The use of dyes to make cell structures more visible under a microscope.
The process by which a cell becomes specialised for a particular function.
An undifferentiated cell that can divide and develop into many different types of specialised cell.
A type of cell division that produces two genetically identical daughter cells, used for growth and repair.
The series of events a cell goes through to grow, replicate its DNA, and divide into two daughter cells.
A thread-like structure made of DNA found in the nucleus, carrying genetic information.
An increase in cell number (by cell division) or cell size as an organism develops.
A stem cell derived from a very early embryo that can differentiate into any type of body cell.
A stem cell found in specific tissues (e.g. bone marrow) that can only differentiate into a limited range of cell types.
The net movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
The movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.
The movement of substances against a concentration gradient, from low to high concentration, using energy from respiration.
The difference in concentration of a substance between two areas — diffusion occurs down this gradient.
A membrane that allows some molecules (e.g. water) to pass through but not others.
The pressure exerted by water inside a plant cell pushing against the cell wall, keeping the cell firm.
The shrinking of a plant cell's cytoplasm away from the cell wall when water is lost by osmosis.
Describes a plant cell that is firm because it has absorbed water by osmosis and the vacuole pushes against the cell wall.
Describes a plant cell that has become limp because it has lost water by osmosis.
The ratio comparing the surface area of a cell to its volume — larger ratios allow faster exchange of substances.
A specialised cell adapted to rapidly transmit electrical impulses around the body. Has a long axon and many dendrites.
A specialised male sex cell adapted for fertilisation — has a tail for movement, many mitochondria for energy, and an acrosome to penetrate the egg.
A specialised female sex cell containing nutrients for the developing embryo and a membrane that changes after fertilisation to prevent further sperm entry.
A specialised plant cell with a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil.
A specialised cell with no nucleus, biconcave shape, and packed with haemoglobin for carrying oxygen around the body.
A cell with tiny hair-like cilia on its surface that beat to move substances, such as mucus in the trachea.
A dead, hollow plant cell reinforced with lignin, forming tubes that transport water and mineral ions up the plant.
